This binding mechanism implies a potential role for Slc22a1 in the pharmacological action of Thioproperazine. The similarity between Imipramine and Clocapramine, both of which are organic heterotricyclic compounds, further supports the idea that they share a common mode of action, possibly involving interactions with Slc22a1. The evidence from the dataset suggests that the relationship between Imipramine and Slc22a1 is mediated through a shared pharmacological profile and a direct interaction with the transporter protein. The integration of these pathways highlights the importance of Slc22a1 in the pharmacological effects of drugs that interact with the nervous system.
